title: Have mercy on me (Psalm 50 [51])
hook: David's psalm after his great sin, prayed every Friday morning

segments.voice: Yesterday, be still: a command spoken in an earthquake. Your line was be still and see. Today, a psalm of sorrow for sin.

A prophet named Nathan walks into the king's palace with a story. Two men lived in a town, he says. One was rich, with flocks and herds. The other was poor, with one little ewe lamb he raised with his children; it ate from his plate and slept in his arms. When a traveler visited, the rich man spared his own sheep, took the poor man's lamb and served it for dinner. King David is furious. That man deserves to die, he says. And Nathan looks at him and says four words.
screen: `A PROPHET WITH A STORY.` → `THE POOR MAN'S ONE LAMB.` → `DAVID IS FURIOUS.`

segments.voice: "Thou art the man." David had taken another man's wife, Bathsheba, and when she was pregnant, he arranged for her husband Uriah to die in battle. He thought it was hidden. Now it's out. David, a king who could have had the prophet killed, says, "I have sinned against the Lord." The heading of Psalm 50 in the Douay, 51 in most Bibles, ties it to this moment. Its Latin first word names it: Miserere, have mercy. "Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy." Nothing held back. It asks to be washed: "Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow." Hyssop, a small plant, sprinkled water in purification rites; that verse is why a priest sprinkling holy water over a congregation is traditionally called the Asperges, from its Latin. The center: "Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels." Create is the Hebrew verb Genesis opens with, and scholars note the Bible uses it only of God. Not a cleaned-up heart: a new one. Near the end, God doesn't want a burnt offering: "a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise." The Church prays this psalm every Friday morning in the Liturgy of the Hours, the day Jesus died. It's also behind Allegri's Miserere, said to have been so guarded by the Sistine Chapel that copies were forbidden, until the young Mozart, the story goes, heard it and wrote it down from memory.
screen: `THOU ART THE MAN.` · `WHITER THAN SNOW.` · `CREATE A CLEAN HEART.` · `EVERY FRIDAY MORNING.`

segments.voice: Let the psalm's first line be the only thing in your mind, slowly, once on each out-breath: have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy. Don't go looking for your worst sin; let the line find whatever needs it. If you pray, stay with those words to God; if you don't, breathe the word mercy, for yourself and someone you find it hard to forgive.
Miserere. Latin for have mercy, the first word and the name of David's psalm after his great sin. Today's word.
Your line: a clean heart. The psalm starts with mercy, not with excuses. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics who pray the Liturgy of the Hours say the Miserere every Friday at Morning Prayer; it is one of the seven penitential psalms, and its verse about hyssop gave its name to the Asperges, the sprinkling with holy water.

notes: Douay wording of 2 Kings 12:7, 12:13 and Psalm 50:3, 9, 12, 19: confirm against a Challoner edition.
Psalm 51 at Friday Morning Prayer in every week of the four-week psalter. Confirm.
Asperges me: the antiphon for the sprinkling rite is Psalm 50:9 (Vulgate). Confirm.
Mozart and Allegri's Miserere (1770, aged 14): famous story, from Leopold Mozart's letters; hedged 'the story goes'. The ban on copies is traditional; confirm.
Hebrew bara (create) used only with God as subject: a standard observation. Confirm.

Review pass: softened "the most complete picture of repentance in the Bible" to "what many readers call the fullest picture" (a judgment, not a settled fact), and hedged the Sistine Chapel ban on copies as "said to have been" in the teach and trapdoor.
David's sin is described as taking another man's wife; some modern readers stress it as an abuse of royal power over Bathsheba. A Keeper may want to review that framing.
